newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki ends off ahead holiday on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki ends off ahead holiday on profit-taking.

text.p: Finnish shares fell on Wednesday, bucking the upbeat sentiment on other European bourses, as profit-taking set in after five days of rises, and because Nokia extended losses after opening lower in New York, brokers said.
Most investors were cautious, or absent, ahead of the Ascension day public and market holiday on Thursday, they said.
Trend-setter Nokia traded in the red the whole session and ended down 5.50 markka at 328.00 after a sell-off in technology stock on Wall Street overnight.
Bank Merita was briefly boosted by higher-than-expected Q1 earnings, but closed down 0.20 markka at 17.80.
"The rise in profits was mostly based on gains from the disposal of equities, so strictly speaking it was not from honest banking operations," one broker said.
"Many have been buying Merita recently, hoping to cash in some hefty profits after its results," another said.
Forestries were soft following a 1.5 percent decline in U.S. paper stocks overnight, and on profit-taking after recent sharp gains. The clearly weaker dollar also hurt, brokers said.
Friday was expected to be quiet. U.S. market reactions to the Fed's Beige Book due for release later on Wednesday would be closely watched, they said.
